RFC2131-2-3.note: Every clause, both producer paths. Server: TestFlagsReservedBitsIgnored sends flags 0 (positive) and 0x7fff (negative) and asserts the reply is unicast to yiaddr:68 either way, so bits 1-15 are ignored; recorded against dhcpserver responseAddr (revert, both polarities). Client acquisition: TestRFC2131ClientSetsReservedFlagsBitsToZero (guest, real client over veth) reads the DISCOVER (positive) and, after an OFFER with flags 0xffff, the REQUEST (negative, bits 1-15 zero); recorded against clearReservedFlags. Client renewal: TestRFC2131ClientRenewalSetsReservedFlagsBitsToZero binds a lease from an ACK with flags 0xffff and a 2 s lease, reads the T1 renewing REQUEST (identified by ciaddr, since NewRenewFromAck copies the ACK xid) and asserts bits 1-15 zero; re-judged 2026-10-18 after renewV4 was replaced by the lease-maintenance loop: the renewing and rebinding REQUESTs are built by v4ExtendRequest, which applies v4RequestModifiers and so clearReservedFlags after NewRenewFromAck, and the record is against v4ExtendRequest (revert). v4ExtendRequest and the acquisition Request are the only client send paths (no release/decline/inform). Records are panic reverts.

RFC2131-3-1.note: positive reads octets 236..239 of OFFER, ACK and NAK and pins 0x63825363; negative replaces the cookie with 0xDEADBEEF and asserts h.handle returns nil

RFC2131-3.2-4.note: positive relays a SELECTING REQUEST with giaddr 192.168.1.254 and asserts responseAddr gives 192.168.1.254:67 for the resulting NAK; negative asserts the same NAK with giaddr zero goes to 255.255.255.255:68, not to a relay

RFC2131-4.1-15.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after ef8666639d). RFC 2131 Section 4.1: "The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first, so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted.  The 'file' field MUST be interpreted next (if the 'option overload' option indicates that the 'file' field contains DHCP options), followed by the 'sname' field." RFC 2132 Section 9.3 values: 1 file, 2 sname, 3 both. findOption reads file only under 52 = 1 or 3, then sname only under 2 or 3. The survivor named by the previous verdict is now killed: ef8666639d adds to TestOverloadAbsentFieldsIgnored a 52=2 packet whose requested address sits in file, asserting it is not read and the request draws a DHCPNAK (tagged negative). Overlay mutants, run under ./le job run: reading file under 52=2 reds that new case (line 197, and the reply turns DHCPACK instead of DHCPNAK at line 204); ignoring 52 reds the positives (TestOverloadFieldsCarryOptions file/sname/both, and line 139); walking sname before file reds TestOverloadInterpretationOrder at line 139 (file copy must win under 52=3). Each field's opening condition and the file-then-sname order are now discriminated in both polarities: 52 absent leaves both unread, 1 leaves sname unread, 2 leaves file unread. Units changed, so this is a fresh judgement, not an upgrade over unchanged units.

RFC2131-4.1-3.note: positive walks each OFFER/ACK/NAK option by its length octets and requires reaching End (255); negative fills a request's options with 0x01 so it carries no End, and requires the reply to be End-terminated

RFC2131-4.1-6.note: positive: TestRFC2131EveryReplyOptionContainedInItsField walks OFFER, ACK and the separately built DHCPNAK by length octets to End inside the options field and requires sname/file all zero with no option 52; TestOptionsContainedWithinTheirField keeps the OFFER/ACK walk. negative: a 300-octet bootfile; judge overlay removing the 255 guard in safeAppendOption reddens it ('option code 98 at offset 555 declares length 98, overrunning the options field'). Receiver side: TestOptionsContainedWithinTheirField negative, an overrunning received option is not read past the field. Config refuses bootfile-bios/uefi over 255 (TestParsePXEConfigInvalid)

RFC2131-4.1-7.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after ef8666639d). RFC 2131 Section 4.1: "The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first, so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted.  The 'file' field MUST be interpreted next (if the 'option overload' option indicates that the 'file' field contains DHCP options), followed by the 'sname' field." findOption walks pkt[240:] first and overloadValue reads option 52 from the options field only; parseMsgType and parseOptionAddr, and h.handle through them, go through findOption. ef8666639d tags the options-first assertion of TestOverloadInterpretationOrder (options, file and sname each carry option 50 under 52=3; the options copy must win) as positive, so the order clause now has a tagged, discriminating assertion beside TestOverloadFieldsCarryOptions (52 interpreted: 53 and 50 in file/sname under 1/2/3 draw a DHCPACK). Negative unchanged: a 52 planted inside file opens no sname. Overlay mutants on options.go, run under ./le job run: walking file before options reds the newly tagged line 131; ignoring 52 reds TestOverloadFieldsCarryOptions (file, sname, both); honouring a 52 found inside file reds the negative at line 150. Recorded breaks are whole-body panics proving reach; these mutants supply the deciding-logic proof. Claims are no wider than the assertions.

RFC2131-4.2-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after ef8666639d). RFC 2131 Section 4.2: "If the client does not provide a 'client identifier' option, the server MUST use the contents of the 'chaddr' field to identify the client." ef8666639d only deletes the stale comment line above TestRFC2131ChaddrContentsIdentifyTheClient that the previous verdict asked removed; no assertion changed. The server reads no option 61 and handle keys every message type on extractMAC (pkt[28:28+hlen]). Overlay mutants on handler.go extractMAC, run under ./le job run: keying on xid reds TestRFC2131ChaddrContentsIdentifyTheClient and TestChaddrIdentifiesClientWithoutClientIdentifier; keying on all but the last chaddr octet reds TestRFC2131ChaddrContentsIdentifyTheClient. Positive (same chaddr, different xid and flags, one client) and negative (one chaddr octet differs, two clients) are distinct assertions.

RFC2131-4.3-1.note: single-polarity positive: option 54 in OFFER, ACK and NAK must equal the server address, so omitting or mis-setting it goes red

RFC2131-4.3-2.note: single-polarity positive: the OFFER's option 51 must be four octets equal to the configured lease seconds

RFC2131-4.3-3.note: single-polarity positive: the ACK answering a DHCPREQUEST must carry option 51 equal to the configured lease seconds

RFC2131-4.3-4.note: positive: the NAK's option walk holds no 51; negative: a REQUEST carrying option 51 that is NAKed still yields a NAK without 51

RFC2131-4.3-5.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 50; negative: requests carrying option 50 still draw OFFER/ACK/NAK without it

RFC2131-4.3-6.note: positive: neither OFFER nor ACK carries option 61; negative: requests carrying option 61 still draw OFFER/ACK without it. The NAK column (MAY) is correctly left unasserted

RFC2131-4.3-7.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 55; negative: requests carrying option 55 still draw replies without it

RFC2131-4.3-8.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 57; negative: requests carrying option 57 still draw replies without it

RFC2131-4.3-9.note: positive and negative both require every NAK option code to be 53 or 54, so any option Table 3 marks 'All others' goes red. The assertion is stricter than Table 3: it would also go red on the Message option (56, SHOULD), Client identifier (61, MAY) and Vendor class identifier (60, MAY), which Table 3 allows in a DHCPNAK

RFC2131-4.3.1-2.note: positive: requested subnet mask, router, DNS and domain name each equal the configured bytes exactly (DNS now byte for byte, closing the length-only gap); negative: a request suggesting other values for all four still gets the configured ones, so a server echoing client-suggested values goes red. {single-polarity} correctly removed from the row

RFC2131-4.3.1-4.note: Forbidden: returning a value for a parameter the server has no value for (neither configured nor a Host Requirements default). TestUnconfiguredParametersOmitted builds a handler with no router, DNS or domain name configured; the negative tag sends a DISCOVER whose parameter request list explicitly names optRouter, optDNS and optDomainName and asserts askedCodes[code] is false for each, so any emitted option for them (including an empty or zero-valued one, since replyOptionCodes records presence by code) goes red. The positive tag asserts the same absence for an unrequested DISCOVER. None of the three has a Host Requirements default, so the ELSE branch applies.

RFC2131-4.3.1-6.note: Forbidden: a requested parameter included more than once in a reply (no option ze emits is one the options document allows to repeat). TestEachParameterEmittedOnce counts every option code in the OFFER and ACK with replyOptionCounts and fails on n != 1 (positive); the negative tag sends a DISCOVER whose parameter request list repeats router, DNS and subnet mask, carries a second PRL and an echoed router option, to both a plain and a PXE server, and fails on any option count other than 1, so a duplicated parameter goes red.

RFC2131-4.4.5-3.note: Server: for leases 60, 3600, 86400 and 604800 the OFFER's option 59 (T2) must be strictly below the lease seconds (positive); parseConfig must reject lease-time 0 (negative). Client, re-judged 2026-10-19 after the DHCPv4 lease loop: TestV4ServerTimersHonoredWhenOrdered calls v4LeaseTimers, the only producer of the client's T2, and asserts a server T2 below the lease (99 s and 95 s in 100 s) is used (positive) and a T2 at the lease (100 s) falls back to both defaults (negative); the default T2 is lease - lease/8 (v4RenewalTimes), below any finite lease. Revert records for both polarities.
